Class EfsFileConnection<E extends IEfsEvent>

java.lang.Object
org.efs.io.EfsFileConnection<E>
Type Parameters:
E - the event type stored and retrieved (must implement IEfsEvent).
public final class EfsFileConnection<E extends IEfsEvent> extends Object
Provides read and/or write access to events in an EfsFile.

An EfsFileConnection is obtained by calling EfsFile.connect(EfsFile.AccessMode, IEfsAgent) and represents a single agent's connection to the file. This connection enforces access permissions (read-only, write-only, or read-write) and manages the lifecycle of event additions and retrieval subscriptions for that agent.

Core Operations

  • Add events: Use add(IEfsEvent) to append a new event to the file (requires write permission). Returns the publish timestamp assigned by the file.
  • Retrieve events: Use retrieve(EfsInterval, Query, Consumer, Consumer) to subscribe to events matching an interval and CQEngine query. Optionally continues delivering future matching events until the interval ends or the subscription is cancelled.
  • Close: Use close() to doClose connection and cancel all active retrieval subscriptions.

Threading and Dispatch

All file operations (add, retrieve, event delivery, and completion notifications) are handed off to the file's dispatcher thread via EfsDispatcher.dispatch(org.efs.dispatcher.EfsAgent). This ensures that all activity on the file appears to be single-threaded from the file's perspective, regardless of the number of connections or agents.

Access Control

The connection's EfsFile.AccessMode determines what operations are allowed:

  • READ_ONLY: only retrieve is allowed; add throws IllegalStateException.
  • WRITE_ONLY: only add is allowed; retrieve throws IllegalStateException.
  • READ_WRITE: both add and retrieve are allowed.

Usage Example


 import org.efs.event.EfsTopicKey;
import org.efs.io.EfsFile;
import org.efs.io.EfsFileConnection;
import org.efs.io.EfsInterval;
import org.efs.io.EfsDurationEndpoint;
import org.efs.io.EfsIntervalEndpoint.Clusivity;
import com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query;
import static com.googlecode.cqengine.query.QueryFactory.all;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;

public class TradeEventExample {
    // 1) Assume dispatcher "tradeDispatcher" exists and is started.
    //    (See EfsDispatcher.Builder example)

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // 2) Create or retrieve topic key for TradeEvent type
        EfsTopicKey<TradeEvent> key = EfsTopicKey.getKey(TradeEvent.class, "trades");

        // 3) Create the event file and assign it to the dispatcher
        EfsFile<TradeEvent> file = EfsFile.createEventFile(key, "tradeDispatcher");

        // 4) Create and register a writer agent
        WriterAgent writerAgent = new WriterAgent("tradeWriter");
        EfsDispatcher.register(writerAgent, "tradeDispatcher");

        // 5) Create and register a reader agent
        ReaderAgent readerAgent = new ReaderAgent("tradeReader");
        EfsDispatcher.register(readerAgent, "tradeDispatcher");

        // 6) Writer agent connects with write access and adds trades
        EfsFileConnection<TradeEvent> writeConn =
            file.connect(EfsFile.AccessMode.WRITE_ONLY, writerAgent);

        // Simulate adding trades
        for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
            TradeEvent trade = new TradeEvent("AAPL", 150.0 + i, 1000L);
            Instant publishedAt = writeConn.add(trade);
            System.out.println("Added trade at " + publishedAt);
        }

        // 7) Reader agent connects with read access and retrieves trades
        EfsFileConnection<TradeEvent> readConn =
            file.connect(EfsFile.AccessMode.READ_ONLY, readerAgent);

        // 8) Build retrieval interval (last 1 hour)
        EfsInterval interval = EfsInterval.builder()
            .beginning(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
                .timeOffset(Duration.ofHours(-1), Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
                .build())
            .ending(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
                .now(Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
                .build())
            .build();

        // 9) Create a CQEngine query to match all trades (or customize to filter)
        Query<EfsRow<TradeEvent>> query = all(TradeEvent.class);

        // 10) Set up latches for synchronization
        CountDownLatch eventLatch = new CountDownLatch(10);
        CountDownLatch completionLatch = new CountDownLatch(1);

        // 11) Retrieve and subscribe to matching trades
        EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<TradeEvent> retrieval = readConn.retrieve(
            interval,
            query,
            row -> {
                // Event callback: handle each matching trade
                TradeEvent trade = row.getEvent();
                System.out.println("Retrieved trade at row " + row.getRowIndex() +
                    ": " + trade.symbol() + " @ $" + trade.price());
                eventLatch.countDown();
            },
            completion -> {
                // Completion callback: handle end of retrieval
                System.out.println("Retrieval completed: " +
                    completion.completionType());
                completionLatch.countDown();
            }
        );

        // 12) Wait for all events to be delivered and retrieval to complete
        eventLatch.await();
        completionLatch.await();
        System.out.println("All trades retrieved and processed.");

        // 13) Cancel retrieval and doClose connections
        retrieval.doClose();  // Cancels if still active; idempotent
        readConn.doClose();
        writeConn.doClose();
        file.doClose();
    }
}

// Simple trade event POJO
static class TradeEvent implements org.efs.event.IEfsEvent {
    private final String symbol;
    private final double price;
    private final long quantity;

    TradeEvent(String symbol, double price, long quantity) {
        this.symbol = symbol;
        this.price = price;
        this.quantity = quantity;
    }

    public String symbol() { return symbol; }
    public double price() { return price; }
    public long quantity() { return quantity; }
}

// Writer agent that publishes trades
static class WriterAgent implements org.efs.dispatcher.IEfsAgent {
    private final String mName;

    WriterAgent(String name) { mName = name; }

    @Override
    public String name() { return mName; }
}

// Reader agent that consumes trades
static class ReaderAgent implements org.efs.dispatcher.IEfsAgent {
    private final String mName;

    ReaderAgent(String name) { mName = name; }

    @Override
    public String name() { return mName; }
}

Key Points

  • All callbacks (event and completion) are dispatched to the agent on its dispatcher thread, not invoked synchronously.
  • Retrieval subscriptions are cancellable via EfsFileConnection.Retrieval.close() and implement AutoCloseable for try-with-resources.
  • Multiple connections (from different agents) may be open on the same EfsFile simultaneously; the file ensures all their operations appear single-threaded.
  • Closing a connection marks it as closed but does not immediately doClose the file; the file remains open until EfsFile.close() is called.

Exception Handling

  • NullPointerException if any required argument is null.
  • IllegalStateException if attempting to add on a read-only connection, retrieve on a write-only connection, or use a closed connection.

    • add

      @Nonnull public Instant add(@Nonnull E event)
      Asynchronously appends given event to underlying EfsFile, assigning it a publish timestamp and a monotonic row index.

      This append is performed as follows:

      1. Validates that the event is not null.
      2. Checks that this connection's access mode is compatible with WRITE_ONLY (i.e., WRITE_ONLY or READ_WRITE); if not, throws IllegalStateException.
      3. Checks that both this connection and underlying file are still open; if not, throws IllegalStateException.
      4. Obtains the current system time from the underlying file's clock.
      5. Wraps the event and timestamp in an AddInternalEvent and dispatches it to the file's dispatcher thread via EfsDispatcher.dispatch(org.efs.dispatcher.EfsAgent), passing the file's EfsFile.onAdd(AddInternalEvent) handler.
      6. Returns the publish timestamp assigned to event.
      7. No user-defined integer tags are associated with this event.

      Threading Model

      Although this method returns immediately with the publish timestamp, the actual row insertion into the file occurs asynchronously on the file's dispatcher thread. This means:

      • Multiple calls to add from the same or different agents will be processed serially on the dispatcher thread in the order posted to event file's event queue.
      • The returned publish timestamp is not guaranteed to be unique; events added in quick succession may receive the same timestamp (the file's clock resolution may be coarser than call frequency).
      • Row indices are guaranteed to be strictly monotonic and unique.
      • Active retrieval subscriptions (see retrieve(org.efs.io.EfsInterval, com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.RetrievalCompleteEvent<E>>)) will receive matching rows as soon as they are inserted, without blocking the caller of this method.

      Event Ordering

      Events added via add are guaranteed to maintain call order in the file: event E0 added before event E1 will receive a smaller row index and (generally) an equal or earlier publish timestamp.

      Access Control

      This method requires the connection to have been opened with write access (WRITE_ONLY or READ_WRITE). Attempting to add on a READ_ONLY connection throws IllegalStateException.

      Error Handling

      Event insertion failures on the dispatcher thread (for example, failure to allocate a row or retrieve time) are not reported back to the caller and do not throw exceptions from this method. The method assumes the dispatcher will log such errors via the file's logger.

      Example
      
 // Assuming 'connection' is an open EfsFileConnection<TradeEvent> with write access
 TradeEvent trade = new TradeEvent("AAPL", 150.25, 1000L);

 try {
     Instant publishedAt = connection.add(trade);
     System.out.println("Trade added at " + publishedAt);
 } catch (IllegalStateException e) {
     System.err.println("Cannot add: " + e.getMessage());
 } catch (NullPointerException e) {
     System.err.println("Trade must not be null");
 }
      Parameters:
      event - the event to append to the file; must not be null and must be an instance of type E.
      Returns:
      publish timestamp assigned to event by event file's clock.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if event is null.
      IllegalStateException - if this connection does not have write access (opened with READ_ONLY mode), or if this connection is closed, or if underlying event file is closed. Also thrown if attempt to postRow retrieval request to EfsFile fails. In all cases, event is not added to event file.
      EfsFileInitializationException - if this event file has a fixed maximum size limit and size policy is EfsFile.SizePolicy.FAIL_ON_LIMIT_REACHED.
      See Also:
      • EfsFile.AccessMode
      • retrieve(EfsInterval, Query, Consumer, Consumer)
      • EfsFile.onAdd(AddInternalEvent)
      • EfsDispatcher.dispatch(org.efs.dispatcher.EfsAgent)

    • add

      @Nonnull public Instant add(@Nonnull Set<Integer> tags, @Nonnull E event)
      Asynchronously appends given event to underlying EfsFile, assigning it a publish timestamp and a monotonic row index.

      This append is performed as follows:

      1. Validates that the event are tags are not null or that tags contains no null values.
      2. Checks that this connection's access mode is compatible with WRITE_ONLY (i.e., WRITE_ONLY or READ_WRITE); if not, throws IllegalStateException.
      3. Checks that both this connection and underlying file are still open; if not, throws IllegalStateException.
      4. Obtains the current system time from the underlying file's clock.
      5. Wraps the event and timestamp in an AddInternalEvent and dispatches it to the file's dispatcher thread via EfsDispatcher.dispatch(org.efs.dispatcher.EfsAgent), passing the file's EfsFile.onAdd(AddInternalEvent) handler.
      6. Returns the publish timestamp assigned to event.

      Threading Model

      Although this method returns immediately with the publish timestamp, the actual row insertion into the file occurs asynchronously on the file's dispatcher thread. This means:

      • Multiple calls to add from the same or different agents will be processed serially on the dispatcher thread in the order posted to event file's event queue.
      • The returned publish timestamp is not guaranteed to be unique; events added in quick succession may receive the same timestamp (the file's clock resolution may be coarser than call frequency).
      • Row indices are guaranteed to be strictly monotonic and unique.
      • Active retrieval subscriptions (see retrieve(org.efs.io.EfsInterval, com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.RetrievalCompleteEvent<E>>)) will receive matching rows as soon as they are inserted, without blocking the caller of this method.

      Event Ordering

      Events added via add are guaranteed to maintain call order in the file: event E0 added before event E1 will receive a smaller row index and (generally) an equal or earlier publish timestamp.

      Access Control

      This method requires the connection to have been opened with write access (WRITE_ONLY or READ_WRITE). Attempting to add on a READ_ONLY connection throws IllegalStateException.

      Error Handling

      Event insertion failures on the dispatcher thread (for example, failure to allocate a row or retrieve time) are not reported back to the caller and do not throw exceptions from this method. The method assumes the dispatcher will log such errors via the file's logger.

      Example
      
 // Assuming 'connection' is an open EfsFileConnection<TradeEvent> with write access
 Set<Integer> tags = new TreeSet<>(List.of(FIRST_TRADE_OF_THE_DAY));
 TradeEvent trade = new TradeEvent("AAPL", 150.25, 1000L);

 try {
     Instant publishedAt = connection.add(tags, trade);
     System.out.println("Trade added at " + publishedAt);
 } catch (IllegalStateException e) {
     System.err.println("Cannot add: " + e.getMessage());
 } catch (NullPointerException e) {
     System.err.println("Trade must not be null");
 }
      Parameters:
      tags - user-defined tags associated with event; must not be null or contain null values. The reason tags are integers and not strings is for faster value comparison.
      event - the event to append to the file; must not be null and must be an instance of type E.
      Returns:
      publish timestamp assigned to event by event file's clock.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either tags or event is null.
      IllegalStateException -
      • if this connection does not have write access (opened with READ_ONLY mode), or
      • if this connection is closed, or
      • if underlying event file is closed, or
      • if underlying event file is full and the file size policy is EfsFile.SizePolicy.FAIL_ON_LIMIT_REACHED, or
      • if attempt to post add request to EfsFile fails.

      In all cases, event is not added to event file.

      EfsFileInitializationException - if this event file has a fixed maximum size limit and size policy is EfsFile.SizePolicy.FAIL_ON_LIMIT_REACHED.

    • retrieve

      @Nonnull public EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<E> retrieve(@Nonnull EfsInterval interval, @Nonnull com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query<EfsRow<E>> query, @Nonnull Consumer<EfsRow<E>> eventCB, @Nonnull Consumer<RetrievalCompleteEvent<E>> completionCB)
      Initiates a retrieval of events from the underlying EfsFile matching the specified interval and CQEngine query, with optional subscription to future matching events.

      This method performs the following:

      1. Validates that all arguments (interval, query, eventCB, completionCB) are not null; throws NullPointerException if any is null.
      2. Checks that this connection's access mode is compatible with READ_ONLY (i.e., READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE); if not, throws IllegalStateException.
      3. Checks that both this connection and the underlying file are still open; if not, throws IllegalStateException.
      4. Creates a new EfsFileConnection.Retrieval instance encapsulating interval, query, callbacks, and agent.
      5. Wraps the Retrieval in a RetrievalInternalEvent and dispatches it to event file's dispatcher thread via EfsDispatcher.dispatch(org.efs.dispatcher.EfsAgent), passing the file's EfsFile.onRetrieve(RetrievalInternalEvent) handler.
      6. Adds the Retrieval to this connection's active retrieval list for cancellation tracking.
      7. Returns Retrieval instance to the caller so events and completion can be received via callbacks, and the retrieval can be cancelled via EfsFileConnection.Retrieval.close().

      Threading Model

      Although this method returns immediately with a Retrieval subscription, the actual query execution and event matching occur asynchronously on the file's dispatcher thread. This means:

      • The eventCB and completionCB callbacks are invoked on the retrieval's agent's dispatcher thread, not from the caller's thread.
      • Events matching the interval and query are delivered to eventCB serially and in ascending row-index order.
      • If the interval includes future events, the retrieval remains active and continues to receive newly inserted events that match the query.
      • When the interval's ending is reached (or retrieval is cancelled), completionCB is invoked exactly once with a RetrievalCompleteEvent describing when the retrieval completed and completion reason.

      Interval and Query Semantics

      The retrieval matches rows from the file as follows:

      • Interval: Defines the begin and end points for row retrieval. Points may be specified by row index, fixed timestamp, or duration offset from current time. See EfsInterval and EfsIntervalEndpoint for endpoint types and clusivity (inclusive/exclusive).
      • Query: A CQEngine Query that further filters rows. Construct queries using CQEngine's QueryFactory methods and obtain field attributes via EfsFile.attribute(String) for the event's fields. A query matching all rows can be created with QueryFactory.all(eventClass).
      • Combined effect: Only rows falling within the interval and matching the query are delivered to eventCB.

      Retrieval Lifecycle
      • Historical events: Rows which exist at the time of retrieval and match the interval and query are delivered first, in increasing row index order.
      • Future events: If the interval extends beyond the current time (see EfsInterval.isFutureInterval(long, java.time.Instant)), the retrieval is registered with the file in order to receive newly added matching rows as they arrive.
      • Completion: The retrieval completes when:
        • All historical rows within the interval have been delivered and the interval does not extend into the future.
        • The retrieval interval's ending point is reached (current time moves past the interval's end).
        • The retrieval is cancelled by the caller via EfsFileConnection.Retrieval.close().
        • The underlying file is closed.
        • This connection is closed.
      • Completion notification: Upon completion, completionCB is invoked exactly once with a RetrievalCompleteEvent specifying completion time and completion type (e.g., RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.RETRIEVAL_COMPLETED, RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.USER_CANCEL, RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.FILE_CLOSED, or RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.CONNECTION_CLOSED).

      Access Control

      This method requires the connection to have been opened with read access (READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE). Attempting to retrieve on a WRITE_ONLY connection throws IllegalStateException.

      Callback Guarantees
      • If eventCB throws an exception, the exception is logged but does not interrupt the retrieval; other matching events continue to be processed.
      • If completionCB throws an exception, the exception is logged but does not prevent the retrieval from closing.
      • Both callbacks are guaranteed to be invoked on agent's dispatcher thread in a single-threaded manner (no concurrent invocations for the same agent).

      Cancellation

      The returned Retrieval is AutoCloseable, allowing try-with-resources usage. Call EfsFileConnection.Retrieval.close() or use try-with-resources to cancel an active retrieval. Cancellation is idempotent: calling doClose() on an already-completed retrieval has no effect.

      WARNING! Because events are retrieved asynchronously, placing a Retrieval instance within a try-with-resources requires the current thread to block until the retrieval completes (effectively turning the asynchronous retrieval into synchronous). Failure to do this results in the retrieval request being closed before the request is processed by the event file.

      Example: Retrieve Historical Events
      // Retrieve all trades from the last hour
EfsInterval interval = EfsInterval.builder()
    .beginning(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .timeOffset(Duration.ofHours(-1), Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
        .build())
    .ending(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .now(Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
        .build())
    .build();

// Create a query that matches trades with price > 150
Query<EfsRow<TradeEvent>> query =
    QueryFactory.greaterThan(file.attribute("price"), 150.0);

try (EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<TradeEvent> retrieval =
    connection.retrieve(
        interval,
        query,
        row -> {
            // Event callback
            TradeEvent trade = row.getEvent();
            System.out.println("Trade: " + trade.symbol() + " @ $" + trade.price());
        },
        completion -> {
            // Completion callback
            System.out.println("Retrieval done: " + completion.completionType());
        }
    )) {
    // Retrieval is active here; callbacks may still be in flight.
    // Try-with-resources will cancel the retrieval when exiting the block.
    // Therefore  a lock-and-condition must be used to prevent retrieval
    // from being canceled.
}
      Example: Subscribe to Future Events
      // Subscribe to all trades starting now and ongoing indefinitely
EfsInterval interval = EfsInterval.builder()
    .beginning(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .now(Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
        .build())
    .ending(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .endNever()  // Interval never ends
        .build())
    .build();

Query<EfsRow<TradeEvent>> query = QueryFactory.all(TradeEvent.class);

EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<TradeEvent> subscription =
    connection.retrieve(
        interval,
        query,
        row -> System.out.println("New trade: " + row.getEvent()),
        completion -> System.out.println("Subscription ended: " + completion.completionType())
    );

// Subscription is now active and will receive all new trades.
// Later, cancel when done:
subscription.doClose();
      Parameters:
      interval - the time or index interval defining the range of rows to retrieve; must not be null. See EfsInterval for details on building intervals.
      query - a CQEngine Query that further filters which rows are delivered; must not be null. Use QueryFactory methods and EfsFile.attribute(String) to construct queries.
      eventCB - a Consumer invoked on the agent's dispatcher thread for each matching EfsRow; must not be null. The callback receives rows in ascending row-index order. Exceptions thrown by this callback are logged but do not interrupt retrieval.
      completionCB - a Consumer invoked exactly once when retrieval completes (either successfully, cancelled, or due to file/connection closure); must not be null. Receives a RetrievalCompleteEvent providing completion time and reason. Invoked on agent's dispatcher thread. Exceptions thrown by this callback are logged but do not prevent the retrieval from closing.
      Returns:
      a EfsFileConnection.Retrieval subscription that can be queried for status or cancelled via EfsFileConnection.Retrieval.close(); never null.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if any of interval, query, eventCB, or completionCB is null.
      IllegalStateException - if this connection does not have read access (opened with WRITE_ONLY mode), if this connection is closed, or if underlying file is closed. Also thrown if attempt to postRow retrieval request to EfsFile fails. In all cases, no events are retrieved from event file.

    • retrieve

      public void retrieve(int tag, @Nonnull Consumer<EfsRow<E>> eventCB, @Nonnull Consumer<RetrievalCompleteEvent<E>> completionCB)
      Retrieves all rows in this file whose tags include the supplied user-defined tag.

      This convenience overload dispatches a tag-based retrieval request to the underlying file and delivers matching rows to the provided event callback in ascending row-index order. It is equivalent to constructing a tag query manually and using the interval-based overload, but it is simpler for the common case of retrieving by a single tag.

      Parameters:
      tag - retrieve events with this user-defined event tag.
      eventCB - a Consumer invoked on the agent's dispatcher thread for each matching EfsRow; must not be null. The callback receives rows in ascending row-index order. Exceptions thrown by this callback are logged but do not interrupt retrieval.
      completionCB - a Consumer invoked exactly once when retrieval completes (either successfully, cancelled, or due to file/connection closure); must not be null. Receives a RetrievalCompleteEvent providing completion time and reason. Invoked on agent's dispatcher thread. Exceptions thrown by this callback are logged but do not prevent the retrieval from closing.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either eventCB or completionCB is null.
      IllegalStateException - if this connection does not have read access (opened with WRITE_ONLY mode), if this connection is closed, or if underlying file is closed. Also thrown if attempt to postRow retrieval request to EfsFile fails. In all cases, no events are retrieved from event file.

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes all active retrieval requests. If this event file is already closed, then does nothing (idempotent).

      This method is asynchronous: it marks the connection as closed and dispatches cancellation events to the file. After this call, no new event adds or retrievals may be created via this connection, but in-flight callbacks may still be processed. Completion callbacks for active retrievals are invoked on the agent's dispatcher thread.
